title: Free a DbContext held by a singleton
summary: A singleton price cache shares one scoped DbContext. Open a scope per lookup, then expire entries with IMemoryCache.

turns.user: prod sometimes throws 'A second operation was started on this context instance'. only at peak hours

assistant.body: TL;DR: the singleton PriceCache is holding on to the scoped ShopDbContext. A DbContext resolved from the root exists only once, so concurrent requests run queries in parallel on the same instance, and DbContext is not thread safe. Scope validation would stop this at startup in Development, but it is off in production. Making PriceCache scoped as well fixes it.

turns.user: wait doesn't that throw the cache away every request? then what's the point of a cache

assistant.body: You are right, and I retract that. A scoped PriceCache is rebuilt per request. Keep it a singleton and create a scope with IServiceScopeFactory only when it has to ask the database, borrowing a DbContext inside it. The long lived object never holds the short lived one directly.

turns.user: prices change, so caching forever is bad. expire after 5 min. oh and admins need to clear one product by hand, forgot to say

assistant.body: Here's the plan: swap the ConcurrentDictionary for IMemoryCache, give each entry an expiry through GetOrCreateAsync, and add Invalidate to drop a single product. Program.cs needs one AddMemoryCache line.

turns.user: sales says 5 min is still too long. 1 min
